fair_value_reason: P/E: NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of about $11.27 (0.25 x FY27 $10.27 + 0.75 x FY28 about $11.6) x 29x (the 4-5-year median forward P/E, about 1 turn below the current 3-year median) = $327. EV/EBITDA: NTM about $4.65B x 18.5x, less about $13.6B net debt, over about 216M shares = about $332. A 50/50 blend gives about $329, vs the agents' mean of $324.8 (their 28-28.5x was justified by a stale 26.4x median, and agents 3 and 4 used FY27 $10.20, which the FY25 conversion precedent does not support). That is about +3.4% plus a 0.2% yield.
supervisor_summary: Round 2 converged hard (fair values $320-329, P(>=318) 0.495-0.545), but mostly because four agents adopted my round-1 FY27 arithmetic and the 26.4x anchor rather than finding independent confirmation. Checking both against primary data: the 26.4x 3-year median is stale (HLT's current 3-5-year forward P/E medians are 29-30x, matching agent 5's Zacks Aug-2026 29.3x), and FY25's +13.9% EPS on +8.6% EBITDA shows 2026's weak conversion was a one-off interest jump, so FY27 sits about $10.27 rather than $10.20. Both point a little higher, so I put fair value at about $329 and lift mid-strike probabilities about 1-1.5 points (P(>=318) 0.535). Bear weights of 17-22% are consistent with a corrected RevPAR base rate (about 18% any decline, about 8% severe), and CoStar's August +2.0% is the expected post-World-Cup run-rate. HLT remains a fairly priced compounder with low-single-digit expected upside.
key_drivers: NUG 6-7% and buybacks (about 4.5% net share shrink) drive EPS: FY25 grew adj. EPS 13.9% on RevPAR +0.4%. FY27 EPS is about $10.2-10.35 (centre $10.27) vs $10.455 consensus, depending on the interest step (+$70-75M) and EBITDA (+8-9%).

Multiple: about 31.5-32x NTM today vs a current 3-year median of about 30x and a 4-5-year median of about 29x. The 26.4x figure covers the 2022-23 trough. The central case assumes about 29x by Sep-2027.
US RevPAR: August +2.0% after a World Cup-boosted June-July. CoStar/TE sees 2027 at +2.1% with GDP accelerating. The June-July 2027 comp is the headwind.

Tail: any annual US RevPAR decline about 18% of years since 1988, a severe (>5%) one about 8%. Non-RevPAR de-ratings (2022: -33%) are the other bear path. In a downturn the buyback (about $3.5B a year at about 3.1x net leverage) is the first lever cut.
